subproblem.title: Localized Besicovitch density: the excess B ∖ A is relatively small at H^n⌞A-a.e. point
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, and let A ⊆ B ⊆ U be Borel sets with H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, where H^n := μHE[n]. Then for H^n⌞A-almost every x (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A)) the following holds for every extended nonnegative real ε ∈ (0, ∞]: there is ρ_ε > 0 such that H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≤ ε · H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ_ε). Equivalently, the inequality holds eventually in the filter 𝓝[>] 0. Products are taken in [0, ∞] with 0 · ∞ = 0. The exceptional H^n⌞A-null set does not depend on ε.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ ε : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μHE[n] ((B \ A) ∩ closedBall x ρ) ≤ ε * μHE[n] (B ∩ closedBall x ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent-supplied proof. These implement Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 87–90 and 113–143). Simon's Upper Density Theorem is replaced by the Besicovitch density theorem: Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.16, which is Mathlib's Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div.
Notation:
- E := Euclid P = ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], μ_A := H^n⌞A = μHE[n].restrict A;
- B̄_ρ(z), B_ρ(z) are the closed and open balls.
Measures of sets lie in [0, ∞], where a/b := a·b⁻¹ with 0⁻¹ = ∞ and ∞⁻¹ = 0; in particular 0/b = 0 for every b.
1. Countable cover. E is a separable metric space; let D ⊆ E be a countable dense set. Let 𝒦 be the family of closed balls B̄_s(q) with q ∈ D, s ∈ ℚ, s > 0 and B̄_s(q) ⊆ U.
- 𝒦 is countable, since it is indexed by a subset of D × ℚ.
- Each K ∈ 𝒦 is closed and bounded in the finite-dimensional space E, hence compact (isCompact_closedBall), and K ⊆ U. So H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis.
- Every z ∈ U lies in the open ball B_s(q) of some B̄_s(q) ∈ 𝒦. Since U is open, choose δ > 0 with B_δ(z) ⊆ U. Choose q ∈ D with |z − q| < δ/4 and a rational s ∈ (δ/4, δ/2). Then |z − q| < s. If |y − q| ≤ s, then |y − z| ≤ s + δ/4 < δ, so B̄_s(q) ⊆ B_δ(z) ⊆ U.
Only these three properties are used below. Any countable family of closed balls inside U whose open balls cover U works equally well, e.g. one obtained from second countability via TopologicalSpace.countable_cover_nhdsWithin.
2. Besicovitch density on one ball. Fix K ∈ 𝒦 and put ν_K := H^n⌞(B ∩ K) = μHE[n].restrict (B ∩ K).
- ν_K(E) = H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞, so ν_K is a finite, hence locally finite, Borel measure on E.
- E is a finite-dimensional real normed space, so it is second countable and has the Besicovitch covering property (instHasBesicovitchCovering).
- By the Besicovitch density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div ν_K A), for ν_K⌞A-a.e. z we have
 Conv_K(z): ν_K(A ∩ B̄_ρ(z)) / ν_K(B̄_ρ(z)) → 1 in [0, ∞] as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
- A, B and K are Borel and A ⊆ B. Applying Measure.restrict_restrict twice gives ν_K⌞A = H^n⌞(A ∩ B ∩ K) = H^n⌞(A ∩ K) = (μ_A)⌞K.
- Hence Conv_K(z) holds for (μ_A)⌞K-a.e. z. Since K is Borel, ae_restrict_iff' turns this into: for μ_A-a.e. z, z ∈ K ⇒ Conv_K(z).
3. One exceptional set. 𝒦 is countable, so the countably many μ_A-a.e. statements of step 2 hold simultaneously (ae_ball_iff): for μ_A-a.e. z, Conv_K(z) holds for every K ∈ 𝒦 with z ∈ K. Moreover μ_A-a.e. z lies in A (ae_restrict_mem, A Borel). Let N be the μ_A-null set where either property fails. N depends on n, U, A and B, but not on ε.
4. Local form of the ratio. Fix x ∉ N.
- x ∈ A ⊆ B ⊆ U, so by step 1 there is K = B̄_s(q) ∈ 𝒦 with x ∈ B_s(q). Put ρ₀ := s − |x − q| > 0.
- For 0 < ρ < ρ₀ and |y − x| ≤ ρ we have |y − q| ≤ ρ + |x − q| < s. So B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ B_s(q) ⊆ K.
- As x ∈ K and x ∉ N, Conv_K(x) holds.
Write a(ρ) := H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)), β(ρ) := H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) and e(ρ) := H^n((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x)). For 0 < ρ < ρ₀:
(i) ν_K(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) = H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ∩ B ∩ K) = a(ρ), since A ⊆ B and B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K;
(ii) ν_K(B̄_ρ(x)) = H^n(B̄_ρ(x) ∩ B ∩ K) = β(ρ), since B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ K;
(iii) β(ρ) ≤ H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞.
The interval (0, ρ₀) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0. On it the quotient in Conv_K(x) equals a(ρ)/β(ρ) by (i)–(ii), so a(ρ)/β(ρ) → 1 as ρ → 0 in 𝓝[>] 0.
(iv) For every ρ, e(ρ) + a(ρ) = β(ρ). The sets (B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and A ∩ B̄_ρ(x) are disjoint, the second is Borel, and their union is B ∩ B̄_ρ(x) because A ⊆ B (measure_union).
5. The estimate. Let ε ∈ (0, ∞].
(a) Case ε ≥ 1. For every ρ, monotonicity ((B ∖ A) ∩ B̄_ρ(x) ⊆ B ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) gives e(ρ) ≤ β(ρ) = 1 · β(ρ) ≤ ε · β(ρ). So the bound holds for all ρ, in particular eventually.
(b) Case ε < 1. Then 1 − ε < 1 (truncated subtraction in [0, ∞]; ε > 0 and 1 ≠ ∞), so (1 − ε, ∞] is a neighbourhood of 1. Since a(ρ)/β(ρ) → 1, there is ρ_ε ∈ (0, ρ₀] such that a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε for all ρ ∈ (0, ρ_ε). Fix such a ρ.
- β(ρ) ≠ 0. Otherwise a(ρ) ≤ β(ρ) = 0 by (iv), so a(ρ)/β(ρ) = 0/0 = 0, contradicting a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε ≥ 0.
- β(ρ) ≠ ∞ by (iii).
- Since 0 < β(ρ) < ∞, the inequality a(ρ)/β(ρ) > 1 − ε is equivalent to (1 − ε)·β(ρ) < a(ρ) (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt).
- Since ε ≤ 1, ε + (1 − ε) = 1. Hence
 e(ρ) + (1 − ε)β(ρ) ≤ e(ρ) + a(ρ) = β(ρ) = ε·β(ρ) + (1 − ε)·β(ρ).
- (1 − ε)β(ρ) < ∞ can be cancelled (ENNReal.le_of_add_le_add_right), giving e(ρ) ≤ ε·β(ρ).
In both cases e(ρ) ≤ ε·β(ρ) holds for all ρ in an interval (0, ρ_ε), that is, eventually in 𝓝[>] 0.
6. Conclusion. Every x ∉ N satisfies the eventual estimate of step 5 for every ε ∈ (0, ∞]. N is μ_A-null and independent of ε, which is the claim. If U = ∅ then A = ∅ and μ_A = 0, so the claim is vacuous; the argument above covers this case as well. ∎
proof_key_steps: A countable family 𝒦 of closed balls B̄_s(q) ⊆ U (compact, so H^n(B ∩ K) < ∞) whose open balls cover U.
Besicovitch density for ν_K = H^n⌞(B ∩ K) holds at ν_K⌞A = (H^n⌞A)⌞K-a.e. point, hence for H^n⌞A-a.e. z ∈ K.
Countable intersection gives one H^n⌞A-null set N, independent of ε, off which x ∈ A and every relevant density ratio tends to 1.
For x ∉ N and small ρ: H^n(A ∩ B̄_ρ)/H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ) → 1, H^n(B ∩ B̄_ρ) < ∞, and e + a = β.
If ε ≥ 1, monotonicity gives e ≤ εβ. If ε < 1, ratio > 1 − ε forces 0 < β < ∞ and (1 − ε)β < a; cancelling gives e ≤ εβ.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and the placement of ∀ ε inside the a.e. conclusion match. The countable compact cover and localized finite-measure density theorem produce one exceptional set. Restriction identities and finite ENNReal cancellation justify the estimate, including zero denominators and ε = ∞. The proof is complete and independent of the parent.
